title: Kundalini: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Kundalini is a traditional image of latent spiritual power, often pictured as coiled. It is not an anatomical structure science has found.

quick_answer.question: What does Kundalini mean?
quick_answer.answer: Kundalini names a latent power in some yogic and tantric traditions. Reports of heat or movement are experiences. They do not establish the picture as physiology.

intro: Kundalini is a religious term for a power said to lie latent and, in many accounts, to rise. The serpent is a metaphor with a history.

sections.heading: What does Kundalini mean?
sections.content:
Tantric and hatha sources supply the image. Modern classes and forums supply symptom lists and a branded yoga. Those layers should stay labeled. Shakti is the broader power language. Chakras are the stations in some maps.

The neighboring page is [what kundalini is](/articles/what-is-kundalini/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
There is no single ancient checklist called an awakening. Intense breathing can create dramatic sensations without confirming a mechanism. The danger page separates risk from mythology.

A wider map lives at the [kundalini topic](/topics/kundalini/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
You can learn the word and decline the chase. If sensations frighten you, see a clinician. Do not pay for a secret that claims to force the process.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [whether it is dangerous](/articles/is-kundalini-dangerous/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not diagnose yourself or anyone else with kundalini. Do not treat the metaphor as an organ. Do not replace medical care with a video.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Kundalini is a traditional term with a narrower meaning than popular English often allows.
Schools and modern classes do not all use it the same way.
The glossary states the limit. Longer pages carry the argument.

faq.question: Is Kundalini a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. It is a traditional concept. Science has not established a serpent energy in the body.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the explainer and the topic pillar.
